SubTopics: Define resources and the cause(s) of their scarcity.
Content: Individuals and societies must make choices regarding which goods and services will be produced and consumed because

A.Choice: unlimited wants can only be satisfied by allocating resources efficiently

B.Choice: resources are insufficient to satisfy the unlimited wants of people

C.Choice: allocating scarce resources efficiently reduces the equitable distribution of goods

D.Choice: income is not equally distributed to ensure that everyone can participate in the market

E.Choice: a country cannot have a comparative advantage in the production of all goods

Content: problems/APMiE/media/2a.jpg
The graph above shows the marginal benefit that a student receives and the marginal cost the student incurs from additional `text(hours)` of study. Which of the following is true?

A.Choice: Beyond `S_2` `text(hours)` of study, there is no further benefit from devoting additional `text(hours)` to study.

B.Choice: At `S_1` `text(hours)` of study, the extra marginal cost of study time exceeds the extra marginal benefit of study time.

C.Choice: The optimal number of `text(hours)` that the student should study is `S_2` `text(hours)`.

E.Choice: The marginal cost of studying decreases as more time is spent studying.

Content: Which of the following occurs if the price of oranges is below the equilibrium price?

A.Choice: There is a surplus of oranges.

B.Choice: The quantity supplied of oranges is greater than the quantity demanded.

C.Choice: The quantity supplied of oranges is greater than the quantity sold.

D.Choice: The quantity purchased of oranges is greater than the quantity sold.

E.Choice: The quantity demanded of oranges is greater than the quantity supplied.

Content: Assume that a `2` `text(percent)` increase in the price of bologna causes a `5` `text(percent)` decrease in the quantity demanded of cheese. What is the cross-price elasticity of demand between these goods, and how are these goods related?

A.Choice: Cross-price elasticity of demand equals `-0.4`, and these goods are complements.

B.Choice: Cross-price elasticity of demand equals `+0.4`, and these goods are substitutes.

C.Choice: Cross-price elasticity of demand equals `-2.5`, and these goods are complements.

D.Choice: Cross-price elasticity of demand equals `+2.5`, and these goods are substitutes.

E.Choice: Cross-price elasticity of demand equals `-0.4`, and these goods are substitutes.

Content: Which of the following is true for a perfectly competitive firm?

A.Choice: The firm is a price taker.

B.Choice: The firm chooses its profit-maximizing quantity by equating price to average total cost.

C.Choice: The firm faces a downward-sloping demand curve for its product.

D.Choice: The firm's short-run supply curve is the same as its average variable cost curve above the minimum of the marginal cost curve.

E.Choice: The firm can expect to earn positive economic profit in long-run equilibrium.

D.Choice: The firm(s) in the industry will charge a price equal to average total cost.

E.Choice: The firm(s) will charge a price on the inelastic portion of the demand curve.

Content: On the island of Gratin, potatoes are produced in a perfectly competitive constant cost industry. The market for potatoes is currently in long-run equilibrium at the market price of `$5` `text(per sack)`.
Draw correctly labeled side-by-side graphs for the potato market and for farmer Lamo and show each of the following.

:ibox:(i) The market equilibrium quantity and price, labeled `Q_M` and `$5`, respectively

(ii) The quantity produced and the price for farmer Lamo, labeled `Q_L` and `$5`, respectively

Believing that the incomes of potato farmers are unfairly low, the government of Gratin imposes a binding price floor at `$7` `text(per sack)`. The government will purchase any surpluses of potatoes. On your graph in part (A), show each of the following.

:ibox:(i) The market quantity of potatoes that would be supplied at the price floor, labeled `Q_F`

(ii) The profit farmer Lamo earns, shaded completely
If the absolute value of the price elasticity of demand is `0.92`, would consumer spending on potatoes increase, decrease, or stay the same as a result of the price floor? Explain.
How would the price floor affect the demand for labor by potato farmers?
Potatoes, corn, and rice are all produced on the island of Gratin in perfectly competitive markets.

:ibox:(i) Assume corn is a substitute in production (an alternate output) for potatoes. How would setting the price floor on potatoes affect the equilibrium price and quantity of corn?

(ii) As a result of an increase in the price of rice, the demand for potatoes increased. Are rice and potatoes substitutes or complements in consumption?
